newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel president shrugs off illness.
newsitem.headline: Israel president shrugs off illness.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman shrugged off a bout of illness at a presidential banquet and planned to continue a hectic tour of India, officials said on Tuesday.
Weizman vomited twice at a Monday night banquet hosted by President Shankar Dayal Sharma and was quickly escorted to his suite at the British-built presidential palace, officials said.
"President Weizman is feeling fine and he is eagerly looking forward to continuing the rest of his programme in India," an Israeli official told Reuters on Tuesday.
It was not clear what caused the illness but an Israeli correspondent accompanying Weizman said two other members of the delegation had taken ill.

One member of the Israeli media accompanying the 72-year-old former air force chief on his first visit to India said he saw Weizman double up with pain as he suddenly began to vomit during the banquet.
"The president vomited twice and was escorted quickly to his room," the media representative said.
But Tuesday was a different story.
Weizman began his schedule with a visit to Delhi's Poosa Institute of Agriculture where he inaugurated an experimental farm to be set up as a joint venture with Israeli help.
"I am happy to bring our modest achievements in agriculture to your great country," he told the meeting that included several farmers. "We are not here to teach you. We are here to cooperate."
He quoted former British prime minister Winston Churchill as saying:" I like to learn. But I hate to be taught."

Weizman's other engagements during the remaining three days of his tour were to include a visit to the Taj Mahal with his wife and a meeting with friends at a southern Indian air base where he served as a British air force pilot in 1946.
He was due to visit a historic synagogue in the southern city of Cochin followed by a meeting with the Indian Jewish community in Bombay on January 3, the last leg of the tour that began on Sunday.
Weizman looked cheerful during a news conference on Monday.
But he showed the odd memory lapse, on one occasion speaking of Lebanon when he meant to give his comments on Hebron.
Weizman fended off a question at Monday's news conference when he was asked if he planned to meet an old girl friend in Bangalore as reported by an Indian newspaper.
"I might be crazy. She might be crazy. I am 72 and she too might be about 70," he said.
